title: Derived tensor product of module objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category whose tensor
product is additive and which has functorial flat resolutions, and let $R$ be a
commutative ring object of $\mathcal C$. The derived category $D(\Mod_R(\mathcal C))$ is
monoidal for the *derived tensor product* $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_RL$. This is the monoidal
structure of [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] for the relative tensor product $\otimes_R$ of
module objects. In particular, for a commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$ and a scheme
$X$, with $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], it is the functor
$$
-\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\times D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X}).
$$

proof.text: Set $\mathcal M=\Mod_R(\mathcal C)$. It is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck]. Closedness and symmetry of $\mathcal C$ make tensoring on either side a left adjoint, so [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] gives preservation of colimits; in particular coequalizers exist and are preserved, as required by [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. That node supplies the relative monoidal structure, and [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] identifies this structure as symmetric and closed. Its tensor functors are therefore left adjoints and preserve finite coproducts by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. A functor between abelian categories preserving zero and finite coproducts preserves the biproduct injections and projections, hence the diagonal and codiagonal; the identity $f+g=\nabla\circ(f\oplus g)\circ\Delta$ then proves its additivity. The functorial flat resolution of $\mathcal C$ induces one for $\mathcal M$ by [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions]. All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal] now hold for $\mathcal M$ with its relative tensor product. Its conclusion supplies precisely the asserted derived monoidal structure, the two-variable left derived tensor, and lax monoidal localization.

source.place: First sentence: hypotheses of the module category and application of the derived-monoidal lemma

proof.text: For the specialization, put $\mathcal S=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, with the sheafified $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Use the small skeleton in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] with $\mathcal A=\Ab$ shows that $\mathcal S$ is Grothendieck abelian and closed symmetric monoidal with additive tensor. The abelian group $\mathbf Z$ is a flat separator: $\mathbf Z\otimes_{\mathbf Z}-$ is the identity and maps from $\mathbf Z$ detect unequal homomorphisms by evaluation at $1$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-flat-separator] gives a flat separator $G$ of $\mathcal S$. Define $P(M)=\coprod_{f:G\to M}G$ and let $\pi_M:P(M)\to M$ have component $f$ on the summand indexed by $f$. A map $u:M\to N$ sends this summand identically to the summand indexed by $uf$, giving a functor and a natural $\pi$. If $a,b:M\to N$ satisfy $a\pi_M=b\pi_M$, their restrictions to every summand give $af=bf$ for every $f:G\to M$, so $a=b$ by the separator property; thus $\pi_M$ is epic. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coproduct], $P(M)$ is flat, so tensoring with $P(M)$ preserves finite limits. Since [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] makes tensoring a left adjoint, it also preserves finite colimits; hence tensoring with $P(M)$ is exact, and symmetry gives exactness in the other variable. This constructs the functorial flat resolution required for $\mathcal S$, without assuming $X$ nonempty or its coefficients finite.

source.place: Second sentence: verification of the sheaf-category hypotheses implicit in the specialization; expanded by the agent using the flat-separator construction

proof.text: For a commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$, [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] gives a commutative ring object $R=\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ in $\mathcal S$. The notation $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ means exactly $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}(\mathcal S)$ by [det-def-sfb-module-objects-sheaves]. Step 2 verifies all assumptions on $\mathcal S$, so step 1 with $(\mathcal C,R)=(\mathcal S,\Lambda_X)$ defines the displayed bifunctor on $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$. Its underived tensor is the relative module tensor used in step 1, so the subscript $\Lambda_X$ specifies this same construction.

The primary declaration is the condensed-coefficient specialization, defined as curriedTensor on DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)). The public import of ModuleObjects.DerivedCategory supplies the general Mod.derivedMonoidalCategory under exactly the closed symmetric monoidal, additive, Grothendieck abelian and functorial-flat-resolution hypotheses.
